record.context_brief: Generalized Pythagorean theorem without dual affine connections
record.original_question: How should one formulate a generalized Pythagorean theorem in a setting where one does not assume a pair of mutually dual affine connections?

evidence.quote: How can we state the generalized Pythagorean theorem if we do not assume a pair of mutually dual affine connections (cf. [25, §22], [21])?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. In classical information geometry, a statistical manifold is endowed with a Riemannian metric $g$ together with a pair of torsion-free affine connections $
abla$ and $
abla^{*}$ that are mutually dual with respect to $g$, meaning that for all vector fields $X,Y,Z$,
$$Xg(Y,Z)=g(
abla_{X}Y,Z)+g(Y,
abla^{*}_{X}Z).$$
For such a dualistic structure, when the manifold is dually flat one can introduce a canonical (Bregman-type) divergence $D$ and prove the generalized Pythagorean theorem: if $p,q,r$ are points such that the $
abla$-geodesic from $q$ to $p$ is $g$-orthogonal at $q$ to the $
abla^{*}$-geodesic from $q$ to $r$, then
$$D(p\,\Vert\,r)=D(p\,\Vert\,q)+D(q\,\Vert\,r).$$

Problem. Formulate and prove an analogue of the generalized Pythagorean theorem in a setting where one is given a smooth manifold equipped with a divergence (or, more generally, a contrast/yoke function) but where one does not assume the existence of a pair of mutually dual affine connections. Specifically, identify intrinsic geometric data (replacing the dual pair $(
abla,
abla^{*})$) — for instance derived directly from the divergence, from a single connection together with auxiliary structure, or from a generalized notion of orthogonality — under which a decomposition identity of Pythagorean type
$$D(p\,\Vert\,r)=D(p\,\Vert\,q)+D(q\,\Vert\,r)$$
(or a suitable generalization thereof) holds for triples $(p,q,r)$ satisfying an appropriate orthogonality condition at $q$.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches reveal numerous formulations of the generalized Pythagorean theorem within the standard dualistic (mutually dual affine connections) framework of information geometry, as well as recent extensions to compactifications of dually flat spaces and to generalized-mean structures. However, no definitive result was located that fully formulates a generalized Pythagorean theorem without assuming a pair of mutually dual affine connections; the question appears to remain open or at most only partially addressed.

status_evidence.title: The generalized Pythagorean theorem on the compactifications of certain dually flat spaces via toric geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Extends the GPT to compactifications of dually flat spaces, still relying on the dualistic structure.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work extends GPT within the dual-connection framework rather than removing the dual-connection assumption.

status_evidence.title: Pythagoras theorem in information geometry and applications to generalized linear models
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Pythagoras theorem assuming a pair of dual connections induced by a divergence.
status_evidence.claim: Standard formulations require the dual connection pair.

status_evidence.title: Information Geometry Associated with Generalized Means
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized-mean information geometries still introduce conjugate/dual connections.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations typically retain a dualistic connection structure.
